subject: On-prem siloed runtime: network and control/data split — readout
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@greenlinehealth.com>, Greenline Health - NetOps <netops@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem siloed runtime: kickoff and network readout request

Hi Elena / NetOps team,

Thanks for taking time today. As discussed in the call, Greenline is targeting a fully isolated on-prem deployment of Redwood Private where the runtime (inference nodes) is strictly segmented from the control plane. Before we move to formal handoff, we'd like to capture a short readout on the proposed network demarc, egress constraints, and canary routing for failover.

Attached is an initial topology PDF (siloed-runtime-topology-v1.pdf) that shows:
- Control plane in a management VLAN with restricted outgoing NAT to our control-plane endpoints (Redwood-managed control cluster).
- Runtime clusters in tenant-specific VLANs with only egress to NAT gateways and a dedicated telemetry relay in the DMZ.
- A lightweight jump-host for certificate/bootstrap that is decommissioned after provisioning.

Specific asks:
1) Can NetOps confirm the feasibility of the proposed asymmetric routing for the canary fallback (runtime -> local egress -> REDWOOD fallback via IPsec to our DR region)?
2) Are there any mandatory BOM items (NAT/routing rules, SNAT pools) we must include in the cutover ticket?
3) Any network security controls that would block our health-check probes (TCP/HTTP to port 8080) between runtime and telemetry relay?

We outlined an acceptance runbook in the Drive link below; happy to iterate. If convenient, please reply with short answers and we can schedule a quick 30-min follow-up.

Thanks,

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenline Health - NetOps <netops@greenlinehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem siloed runtime: kickoff and network readout request

Priyom,

Thanks — reviewed the topology. High level answers:
1) Asymmetric routing for the canary fallback is acceptable but we need to terminate IPsec at our DR egress node. We can create a managed tunnel to Redwood DR as long as you provide the peer IPs and pre-shared key rotation schedule.
2) BOM: please include two SNAT pools (primary/standby), explicit /32 entries for control-plane endpoints to avoid accidental SNAT collisions, and ACL entries that allow outbound to Redwood telemetry endpoint FQDNs (we'll handle IPs via DNS ACLs).
3) Health checks: port 8080 outbound is fine but our proxy will rewrite some headers; ensure probes are resilient to 302s. Also, telemetry TLS mutual-auth is required for ingestion.

I'll have NetOps open a ticket with the required cross-connects and a timeline for the IPsec termination.

- Elena
NetOps Lead, Greenline Health
elena.ramos@greenlinehealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 13:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem siloed runtime: kickoff and network readout request

Thanks Elena — quick clarification and notes from the infra side:

- IPsec: we will provide the peer IPs and a short-lived PSK process. Kimberly, please confirm the key-rotation TTL we can commit to for the POC (we typically scope 30d keys for POC and 7d for production).
- SNAT pools: agree with two pools. For routing, we'd like to avoid hairpin NAT for telemetry so runtime should route telemetry to the DMZ relay (no SNAT) when possible; fall back to SNAT only on cross-datacenter failover. That reduces source preservation issues for your ingress filters.
- Telemetry mutual TLS: we'll support mTLS. We'll need an API to upload CA bundles during onboarding — Irene, can your team expose a short-lived upload endpoint scoped to the provisioning job?

Attachments: I appended a short canary egress playbook (canary-egress-playbook.md) that outlines the failover steps and health-check expectations.

Next steps: can NetOps propose preferred IPsec termination nodes and a tentative cutover weekend? If so, we'll draft the cutover ticket and include runbook steps.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@greenlinehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem siloed runtime: kickoff and network readout request

Elena / NetOps,

Appreciate the quick review and the clear BOM. A short summary from Redwood's side and decisions we propose for the cutover ticket:

1) IPsec termination: Redwood will accept IPsec to a single DR egress node for the POC. We'll supply the peer IP and the initial PSK by EOD Thursday. Production will expand to two tunnels for HA.
2) SNAT pools & routing: we'll include two SNAT pools in the ticket. The runtime will prefer DMZ relay with preserved source for telemetry. Canary routing will use IP routing + route preference changes (no NAT) until explicit failover is invoked.
3) Health checks & mTLS: runtime health probes will tolerate 302s; telemetry will use mTLS with CA bundle upload via a time-limited signed URL (Irene to create).

Cutover weekend proposal: 2026-12-18 to 2026-12-19 with a dry-run on 2026-12-15. Can NetOps confirm availability?

I'll include the attachments and the Drive link in the cutover ticket. If there are any policy blockers from your side, flag them and we'll address in the follow-up.

Thanks,

--
Kimberly Park
Security & Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
